transcript.content: Hello. I am Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that my eating has just gotten really off lately. Some days I barely get down a cup of coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift. And I've noticed my scrubs have been hanging pretty loose on me, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight at all. So, I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you feel like your body weight or shape is a problem for you?

No, not at all. I don't have any issues with my weight or shape. Like I was saying, I'm really not trying to lose weight. When I look in the mirror, I just see myself... maybe looking a little more run down or tired lately. But I don't think I'm overweight or anything like that. I just really don't have an appetite.
Beyond your lack of appetite, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I have. Honestly, most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's just... like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. And that feeling just kind of stays with me most of the day.
Have you ever felt this way for an extended period of time in the past, or is this the first time you have experienced these symptoms?

Well, I've had some other things going on in the past, but this steady depression and just... loss of interest in everything, that settled in later. It's been with me for roughly the past year and four months now. So yeah, it's been going on for a while.
During these past sixteen months, has there ever been a period of two months or longer where you felt completely like yourself and free of these symptoms?

No, not really. For most of this whole stretch, I've been living with that heavy, hollow mood and the loss of interest. It hasn't just been a few bad weeks here and there... it's been pretty constant. I don't think I've had a break from it for two months straight, no.

During this period, have you ever experienced a time where your mood was unusually high, energetic, or irritable to the point where you felt like you didn't need much sleep and were doing much more than usual?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I've just been feeling really down and tired, like I said. I definitely haven't had any extra energy or felt like I didn't need sleep. If anything, I just want to sleep more.
Have you noticed any difficulty with your concentration or ability to make decisions since you've been feeling this way?

No, not really. I haven't noticed any problems with my concentration. I mean, I'm definitely tired, but I can still focus on what I need to do at work and things like that. And making decisions hasn't been an issue either. It's really just the mood that's the problem, not my thinking.
Do you often feel bad about yourself or feel like you are inadequate?

Yeah, I do. I just... I keep thinking I'm a burden, you know? To the clinic where I work, and to my family. It's like every little thing I do wrong is a huge deal. Like, if I'm a little slow turning over a patient room, I just blame myself so much. I feel like I've ruined everyone's whole day just because of a small delay. It just feels like I'm not doing a good enough job anywhere.
Do you often find yourself feeling hopeless about the future?

Yeah, I do. It's just hard to see things getting better. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling... it's like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. When every single day starts out like that, it's pretty hard to feel hopeful about what's ahead.
Over the past sixteen months, have you generally felt that you have low self-esteem?

I wouldn't say I've felt that way for that long. I mean, I've had these feelings of being a burden lately, like I mentioned, but it hasn't been a constant thing for the last year and a half. It's more of a recent issue with my mood, really.
Over the past sixteen months, have you felt physically tired or low on energy most of the time?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's been pretty constant. Even if I get a full night's sleep and stay in bed the whole time, I wake up and my body just feels... heavy. Like I just finished a double shift at the clinic or something. And it doesn't get better. By lunchtime, I'm just fighting to keep my eyes open and keep my thoughts together. It's just a real struggle to get through the day with how tired I am.

During these past sixteen months, have you ever experienced a period of two weeks or longer where your mood was so low that you lost interest in almost all of your usual activities, beyond what you have been experiencing on a daily basis?

Yes, definitely. There was a stretch not too long ago where it got really bad. I mean, I used to go running in Van Cortlandt Park, take photos, and meet up with friends to play chess. But during that time... and honestly, even now sometimes... I just lost all interest. I'd tell myself there was no point in doing any of it. I'd just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or staring at my budget spreadsheet instead of actually doing anything I used to enjoy.
